headline: Marie-Antoinette Porcelain Bowl Sells For Record 3.1 Million Dollars
metaDescription: A rare porcelain bowl commissioned by King Louis XVI for Marie-Antoinette sold for a record 3.1 million dollars at an auction held in Paris on Thursday.
aiSummaryBullets: A porcelain bowl historically linked to Marie-Antoinette was sold at a Paris auction for 3.1 million dollars.
The item, known as a jatte-teton, was originally commissioned by King Louis XVI for the queen's royal dairy.
The sale represents a record price for any Sèvres porcelain work ever sold at auction.
aiContextParagraph: A 18th-century porcelain bowl belonging to the late French Queen Marie-Antoinette was purchased at a Paris auction on Thursday for a record-breaking 3.1 million dollars. Known as a jatte-teton, or nipple bowl, the piece was part of a set of four commissioned by King Louis XVI during the pre-revolutionary period. The items were created for the queen's royal dairy creamery, a site intended to represent the idealized pastoral life that Marie-Antoinette enjoyed. The auction results mark the highest price ever paid for a Sèvres porcelain work in history. The provenance of these bowls is tied to the French monarchy before the onset of the Revolution. The sale highlights the ongoing interest in royal artifacts from this era, with current valuations for such historical pieces continuing to reach significant figures among private collectors and institutions worldwide.
whyItIsViral: The event is covered by two independent media outlets, reflecting notable interest in historical royal artifacts.
